punchline: Carol Dweck set out to study how children cope with failure and found some who didn't see it as failure at all.
thirty_sec: As a young researcher, Carol Dweck gave children puzzles that got harder until they couldn't solve them, expecting to study how they coped with failure. Instead, one ten-year-old rubbed his hands together and shouted, 'I love a challenge!' Another said he'd hoped it would be informative. They weren't failing, they believed. They were learning. That surprise launched her research on fixed and growth mindsets.
question: What's something hard that turned out to be more informative than you expected?
